name: Crown Castle
description: Crown Castle is a tower REIT: it owns more than 40,000 U.S. cell towers and rents antenna space to wireless carriers under long-term contracts, with built-in rent escalators and very low incremental cost per added tenant. T-Mobile, AT&T and Verizon were about 90% of 2025 site rental revenue, so carrier consolidation and defaults matter. It sold its small-cell and fiber business (about 105,000 small cell nodes and 90,000 fiber route miles) to EQT and Zayo for $8.5B gross, closed May 1, 2026, becoming a pure tower company; it plans to repay about $7B of debt and buy back about $1B of stock. Its biggest near-term problem is DISH (EchoStar), which stopped paying: Crown Castle terminated the contract in January 2026, asserts more than $3.5B is owed, and expects about $220M less 2026 site rental revenue.

gics.note: Conventional GICS sector and sub-industry as listed in Wikipedia's List of S&P 500 companies (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_S%26P_500_companies), read 2026-10-01; industry group and industry are not shown there. SEC SIC 6798 (Real Estate Investment Trusts).

employees.note: approximately 4,000 including about 2,500 in discontinued operations (the fiber and small cell business sold May 1, 2026)

businessLines.name: Site rental (towers)
businessLines.how: Recurring rent from long-term tenant contracts (lease, license, sublease) with annual escalators; adding tenants to existing towers is high-margin because costs are largely fixed ground rent and maintenance.
businessLines.description: Space on more than 40,000 towers and rooftops, leased to wireless carriers; 95% of net revenues. T-Mobile, AT&T and Verizon about 90% of site rental revenue.

businessLines.name: Services and other
businessLines.how: Fees per project (site acquisition, engineering, zoning and permitting) for carrier tenants adding equipment.
businessLines.description: Mainly pre-construction site development services (installation services discontinued in 2023 restructuring).

whatsNext.text: FCC Trust Order (May 12, 2026) required EchoStar to fund a $2.4B trust (established July 28, 2026) for qualified claims; Crown Castle believes its DISH master lease claims (asserted more than $3.5B) qualify, subject to trust rules and available assets
2026 Restructuring Plan (Feb 2026) targeting about $65M annualized operating cost savings in the tower business
